evidence.claim: Old Lyme’s scenic section of US 1 runs 0.96 mile between the Lieutenant River and Griswold Avenue, designated by Connecticut in 2012.
evidence.quote: a 0.96 mile section in Old Lyme between the Lieutenant River and Griswold Avenue (designated in 2012).

evidence.claim: At the river end, a tidal waterway joins the Connecticut River’s estuary just above Long Island Sound.
evidence.quote: The Lieutenant River is a 3.7-mile-long (6.0 km) tidal river located in Old Lyme, Connecticut.  It joins the Connecticut River in the estuary, just above the point where that river flows into Long Island Sound.

evidence.claim: US 1 generally follows the Boston Post Road and the turnpikes built to replace it; the New London and Lyme Turnpike connected Old Lyme with New London in 1807.
evidence.quote: US 1 generally follows the old Boston Post Road and turnpike roads built to replace it.

evidence.claim: the New London and Lyme Turnpike connected Old Lyme with New London in 1807.
evidence.quote: the New London and Lyme Turnpike (1807) connected Old Lyme with New London.

evidence.claim: In Old Lyme and East Lyme, US 1 shifted onto the line now used by I-95 from 1949 to 1976.
evidence.quote: from 1949 to 1976, US 1 existed where I-95 currently exists in Old Lyme and East Lyme.

evidence.claim: It returned to the 9.4-mile Boston Post Road stretch in 1976, replacing Route 51.
evidence.quote: In 1976, US 1 returned to the 9.4-mile (15.1 km) stretch of road, thus eliminating the need for Route 51.

evidence.claim: Begin with the Lieutenant River and continue toward Griswold Avenue.
evidence.quote: a 0.96 mile section in Old Lyme between the Lieutenant River and Griswold Avenue

evidence.claim: The Florence Griswold Museum on Lyme Street preserves the boardinghouse where American Impressionists painted on walls and doors.
evidence.quote: The Florence Griswold House in Old Lyme, Connecticut was a boardinghouse run by Florence Griswold, where American Impressionist artists lived and painted—often directly on the walls and doors of the house.

evidence.claim: The Florence Griswold Museum on Lyme Street
evidence.quote: The Florence Griswold Museum is an art museum at 96 Lyme Street in Old Lyme, Connecticut

evidence.claim: At Sill Lane’s junction with the Post Road, Peck Tavern is now a private residence.
evidence.quote: The Peck Tavern is a historic tavern (now a private residence) at 1 Sill Lane in Old Lyme, Connecticut.

evidence.claim: At Sill Lane’s junction with the Post Road
evidence.quote: at center of the triangular junction of Sill Lane and Boston Post Road (Route 1).

evidence.claim: The Lieutenant River meets the Connecticut River in its estuary, just above Long Island Sound.
evidence.quote: It joins the Connecticut River in the estuary, just above the point where that river flows into Long Island Sound.

evidence.claim: This 3.7-mile tidal river became a subject for American Impressionists, including Childe Hassam, while they stayed at the Florence Griswold House.
evidence.quote: The Lieutenant River is a 3.7-mile-long (6.0 km) tidal river located in Old Lyme, Connecticut.

evidence.claim: became a subject for American Impressionists, including Childe Hassam, while they stayed at the Florence Griswold House.
evidence.quote: A number of American impressionist artists, including Childe Hassam, painted views of the river while staying at the Florence Griswold House in Old Lyme.

evidence.claim: The museum’s windows look onto the river, connecting its setting with the landscape those artists painted.
evidence.quote: The Florence Griswold Museum was designed with windows that have  sweeping views of the Lieutenant River.

evidence.claim: Forty-one painted panels occupy the downstairs rooms of Florence Griswold’s former boardinghouse.
evidence.quote: A total of 41 painted panels are in the downstairs rooms.

evidence.claim: Her artist-boarders made the dining room’s walls and doors into a showcase for their work.
evidence.quote: The house's dining room, where artists would gather to debate topics of the day, became a showcase for painted wall and door panels created by the artist-boarders.

evidence.claim: Matilda Browne was the only woman invited to contribute a panel; she painted Griswold’s bedroom door.
evidence.quote: Matilda Browne was the only female artist invited to contribute a panel and was given a place of honor: Miss Florence's own bedroom door.

evidence.claim: The house became a center of the Old Lyme Art Colony, whose members helped develop American Impressionism.
evidence.quote: The house was once the epicenter of the Old Lyme Art Colony whose members (many of whom were Griswold's boarders) played an important role in the development of American Impressionism.

evidence.claim: Harry Hoffman, an Old Lyme resident, helped save it through a fundraising campaign for its conversion into a museum.
evidence.quote: Old Lyme resident Harry Hoffman helped to save Griswold's house through a fund-raising campaign so that it could be converted into a Museum.

evidence.claim: The first floor is furnished to reflect about 1910, the height of its boardinghouse years.
evidence.quote: The entire first floor has been furnished to reflect its appearance in about 1910, the height of its years as an artists' boardinghouse.

evidence.claim: Peck Tavern occupies the triangular junction of Sill Lane and Boston Post Road, at the northern end of Old Lyme’s historic village center.
evidence.quote: The Peck Tavern is located at the northern end of Old Lyme's historic village center, at center of the triangular junction of Sill Lane and Boston Post Road (Route 1).

evidence.claim: The former tavern is now a private residence.
evidence.quote: The Peck Tavern is a historic tavern (now a private residence)

evidence.claim: Its clapboard exterior has a projecting central entrance section rising two stories, with a transom window above the door.
evidence.quote: The main (south-facing) facade is five bays wide, with the center bay consisting of a two-story gable-topped projecting section.  The main entry is in this section, flanked by fluted pilasters and topped by a transom window.

evidence.claim: Its clapboard exterior
evidence.quote: wooden clapboard siding

evidence.claim: The property served travelers into the early 19th century as a major stop on the post road, which was later upgraded to a turnpike.
evidence.quote: The property was used as a tavern into the early 19th century, serving as a major stop on the early post road, which was later upgrade to a turnpike and saw a great deal of traffic.

evidence.claim: Inside, a surviving taproom contains the original 18th-century sign, remnants of the building’s former work as a tavern.
evidence.quote: Among the building's unique interior features are a surviving taproom from its use as a tavern, with the original 18th-century sign on display there.
